en.title: Goldman Sachs OA #1: Autocorrect Prototype
en.description:
Implement an autocorrect feature: given a word list words and a number of queries queries, for each query return all words in the list that are anagrams of it, sorted in ascending lexicographic order.

An anagram is a string formed by rearranging the letters of another string; the count of each letter must be exactly the same. A word identical to the query also counts.
en.input:
The first line contains an integer n, followed by n lines, each containing one word. The next line contains an integer q, followed by q lines, each containing one query.

1≤n≤750, 1≤q≤750; each word and query has length 1..100 and contains only lowercase English letters; the words in the list are distinct; every query is guaranteed to have at least one anagram in the list.
en.output: Output q lines. Line i first gives the number k of results for query i, then the k words in ascending lexicographic order, separated by spaces.
en.explanation:
Example 1: the only anagram of spede is speed; the anagrams of deul are duel and dule. cars is not an anagram of any query.
Example 2: listen, silent, enlist, and tinsel are anagrams of one another and are output in lexicographic order; google and elgoog both map to google.
Example 3: aab and abb use the same letters but with different counts, so they are not anagrams; the result for query ab includes the identical word ab.
hints: Use a word's sorted characters as its signature; anagrams share the same signature.
Group words by signature in a hash map; each group only needs to be sorted once.
Words identical to the query must also be output.
